text:
The ratio of atoms in two energy levels follows the Boltzmann equation:

n₂/n₁ = (g₂/g₁) exp(-ΔE/kT)

The ratio we're interested in changes with temperature. Taking the ratio of this ratio (no spots to spots):

R(no spots)/R(spots) = exp(-ΔE/kT₁) / exp(-ΔE/kT₂)

where T₁ = 6000 K (no spots) and T₂ = 5500 K (spots). The g₂/g₁ factors cancel.

R(no spots)/R(spots) = exp[-ΔE/k · (1/T₁ - 1/T₂)]
= exp[(ΔE/k) · (1/T₂ - 1/T₁)]

Calculate ΔE from wavelength λ = 1448 Å:

ΔE = hc/λ = (6.626×10⁻³⁴ × 3×10⁸)/(1448×10⁻¹⁰)
= (1.9878×10⁻²⁵)/(1.448×10⁻⁷)
= 1.373×10⁻¹⁸ J

ΔE/k = 1.373×10⁻¹⁸ / 1.381×10⁻²³ = 9.94×10⁴ K

Calculate the temperature factor:
1/T₂ - 1/T₁ = 1/5500 - 1/6000 = 1.818×10⁻⁴ - 1.667×10⁻⁴ = 1.515×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹

Exponent = 9.94×10⁴ × 1.515×10⁻⁵ = 1.506

R(no spots)/R(spots) = exp(1.506) = 4.51

This matches option (D).

Answer: D
